EPILOGUE
✦Player One

Series bible

1. Title and Logline

Title: UNWEPT Format: Full-color vertical-scroll series, 40 chapters in 4 arcs, with a complete ending.

Logline: A speedrunner who never cried at his mother's funeral dies at the last frame of her unfinished game. He wakes outside humanity's last lit city inside the corpse of an exiled "powerless" boy. There he has to hide the monster he is turning into while he finds out why the system that ranks every human plays the same level-up chime his mother wrote.

2. The World

Orison

Orison is a continent drowned in grief. Three centuries ago its Seven Crowns fought each other with Thrumcraft. Thrum is the living energy of emotion, so the more you felt, the harder you hit: grief worked as gravity and rage burned as fire. At the Battle of the Kessary Basin, a queen's grief for her dead son set off a chain reaction called the Unmaking, and feeling became weather. Emotion-storms flattened every city. When they settled, the land lay under the Spill, a black-violet mist of condensed despair beneath a permanently bruise-colored sky.

The legend says that "a woman fell from the sky, weeping" into the Kessary crater. People call her the Wickmother. She grew a spire of white-gold crystal called the Wick, gave the survivors the Tally, raised the Pale, wrote the Lit Charter and founded Lanthorn. In Year 97 she "ascended into the Wick." The story opens in Year 312 of the Lit Reckoning.

Lanthorn, the Last Lit City

  • About 400,000 people live inside the Pale, a dome-wall of white light 12 km in radius that pulses every six seconds. Inside it the Wick makes artificial daylight. Outside there is only the Spill, drowned ruins and monsters.
  • The districts form concentric rings. The Crown sits at the center and holds the Concord and the Wick. Around it are the Lantern Ward (the elite), the Kindle Ward (artisans and Lanternhall Academy), the Tinder Ward (laborers and the Wick-works), and the Fringe (barracks, fungus farms and bell towers) pressed against the Pale.
  • Grade decides your life: housing, rations, marriage and votes. Every child receives a Tally at 12. Anyone still Unlit (Null) at 16 is Snuffed, which means being walked through the Pale at dawn carrying an unlit lantern. No Snuffed Null has ever come back.

Factions

Faction Description
The Concord Seven Pyre-grade elders who rule from the Crown, led by High Tallier Severin Ashgrave. They control the Wick, the Grades and the once-a-decade Harvest.
The Auditors Concord secret police in gray coats with glowing blue lens-visors. Their True Read detects "Discrepancies," meaning anomalies in a person's Tally.
The Vigil The army that guards the Pale and reaps monsters. It trains cadets at Lanternhall.
The Wick-works The engineers' guild that maintains the Wick's machinery. They know the pipes but not what flows through them.
The Wracks The monster-tide of the Spill.
The Unwept A handful of ancient, intelligent Wracks, led by Tomorrow.
The Unlit Snuffed Nulls who secretly survived in the ruins. They are starving and hunted, and some are half-mad.
The Order of the Hush Starts as one fan's secret club and ends as a real spy network.

The Central Mystery

Where do Wracks come from, and why do they throw themselves at the Pale? Why does no Snuffed Null ever return? What really happened to the Wickmother? And a question only Jonah can ask: why does the Tally's level-up chime (TING-TA-LING) match the one his dead mother composed?

The True Answer, Revealed in Layers

  1. Arc 1: Wracks are made of the feelings of Lanthorn's living citizens. Each Wrack's core, called a Knot, holds one specific person's unfelt emotion and the memory attached to it. That person is still alive inside the Pale and no longer remembers it.
  2. Arc 2: The Tally is a siphon. It takes a share of each citizen's heavy emotions (grief, fear, rage, shame, envy), called their Yield, and pays it back as stable, numbered power. Promotion to a higher Grade secretly requires a deeper Yield, so the higher your Grade, the emptier you are. The siphoned feeling runs through conduits under the city and vents beyond the Pale at the Weeping Vents, where it condenses into Wracks. Wracks swarm the Pale because feeling seeks its owner. Reaping them sends the energy back into the Wick, which closes the loop. The Concord schedules the Harvests. The war is a farm.
  3. Arc 3: The Wickmother is Miriam Reed, Jonah's mother. She was an Earth game designer who died of an aneurysm and fell into Orison 312 years ago, because souls fall through the dark at different speeds. She built the Tally from her unfinished game as an emergency measure against the Unmaking and tried to shut it down in Year 97. Her first student, Severin, sealed her alive in the Wick as its living core. She left backdoors behind: the Pardon of Thirty Nights, Article Zero, and the Undertally, which is her game's old secret debug menu rebuilt and keyed to her son's soul. When Jonah died, she caught his soul. Nulls are exiled because Article Zero would let any Null challenge the system's master.
  4. Arc 4: Jonah's suppression was the villain's fuel. Severin engineered the Harvest to make the Null Capsize, because only an unsiphoned Capsize is strong enough to ignite the Final Tally. The Final Tally is a permanent siphon of all human feeling. It would end Wracks forever, leave humanity calm and empty, and make Severin a Zenith.

The real enemy is not the monsters. It is a civilization that exported its pain instead of feeling it, and the man who refuses to let that stop.

  • The six-level prototype (Ch 1) → the Wick's six tiers (Ch 36)
3. The Progression System: The Tally

How It Works

Citizens touch a shard of the Wick at age 12 and receive a holographic status window. It shows Level, Grade, five attributes (Might, Grace, Focus, Resolve, Resonance), a Thrum pool, Skills and Tethers. - Marks (experience points) come from Reaping, which means shattering a Wrack's Knot. - Skills are Inscribed from the Lattice, a branching skill tree, at each level-up. - Grade promotion requires a Grading Rite. Publicly it is a test of talent. Secretly it takes a deeper Yield. Anyone who refuses is capped at the top of their Grade for life. - Overdrawing your Thrum causes a Gutter, an instant collapse.

Grade Levels Hidden Yield Gate Examples
Unlit (Null) — 0% (cannot Yield) Snuffed at 16
Tinder 1–9 5% Otto (Lv 6)
Kindle 10–24 15% June (Lv 14)
Taper 25–39 30% —
Lantern 40–59 45% Dorian (Lv 44)
Beacon 60–79 60% Solenne (Lv 63), Iona (Lv 79, capped by choice)
Pyre 80–99 80% Concord elders, Severin (Lv 99)
Zenith 100 100% + a Harvest Only the Wickmother has ever reached it

Tethers: Restrictions That Make You Stronger

  1. You declare a Tether during 10 seconds of uninterrupted stillness outside combat. It stays bound until you release it at dawn, and it can never be loosened mid-fight.
  2. A skill can hold at most three Tethers. Contradictory Tethers cancel each other.
  3. Difficulty pricing: the Tally sets each Tether's multiplier by how often an average person would fail it. Easy conditions give about ×1.1. Brutal ones give ×10 or more.
  4. Breaking a bound Tether causes a Snap, a backlash scaled to its multiplier: Thrum burn, the skill sealed for a day, or internal injury.
  5. A Tether can only bind your own body and actions.

Stakefire: Disputes Settled by Contest

  1. The challenger names stakes. The challenged names counter-stakes and writes the rules.
  2. The Tally weighs both stakes for proportion, and a gold flame ignites between the parties.
  3. The rules are enforced as written, never as intended.
  4. The loser's stake "burns." Grades, skills, oaths, exile and even memories can be transferred or erased.
  5. Anyone may refuse a Stakefire, with one exception. Article Zero of the Lit Charter says: "No Stakefire offered by the Unlit may be refused." Everyone considers it a dead letter, since Nulls are exiled.

The Undertally (Jonah Only)

This hidden layer opens when he first gnaws a Knot. Other Nulls can learn its techniques, but only he has the window. - Gnaw: absorb a Knot and gain that emotion's skill. While a Knot is Undigested it gives raw, unstable power and adds Undertow. - Digest: relive the Knot's memory and actually feel it. The skill becomes permanent and refined, Undertow drops and Depth rises. Digesting takes hours and leaves him vulnerable, and early on his own suppression blocks it. - UNDERTOW (pressure): - Rises when he suppresses a strong feeling, carries Undigested Knots, or stays in monster form (until Maelstrom Knight). - Falls when he digests Knots or expresses a feeling honestly: says it, laughs, shouts or weeps. - Thresholds: at 25% Wracks read him as kin. At 50% his eyes glow violet and monster features leak through. At 75% Knot-voices whisper and his Tethers strain. At 100% he CAPSIZES: he becomes an uncontrolled colossus. Afterward comes the Crash, which resets Undertow to about 40% and halves his stats for days. - The trap: a hidden Pressure Bonus adds 1% damage for every 1% of Undertow. Suppression makes him stronger, until it destroys him. - DEPTH (unlocks in Ch 23): stable, permanent power earned from digested feeling. It boosts every stat and can never be lost. Eventually it is strong enough to absorb a Snap.

How Jonah Breaks and Bends the System

  1. Difficulty arbitrage. The Tally prices Tethers for average humans, and he has frame-perfect timing. The Window ("this strike only lands in the 3 frames after the enemy commits") is worth ×9 to him at almost no risk.
  2. Stillness. "While my expression does not change, all damage ×2." His resting face is effectively a build. The Bread Clause (×1.5 while holding food) explains why he is always holding bread.
  3. Frame exploits. He clips through a 3-frame gap in the Pale's refresh, cancels skill recovery with Blink, uses invulnerability frames and takes deliberate hits to cross gaps.
  4. Rules as written. He reads Stakefire contracts like game manuals and finds the loopholes.
  5. Counterfeit. A forged blank UNLIT window hides the Undertally from Auditors.
  6. Off-ladder growth. His Knot evolutions skip the Grade system entirely.
  7. His mother's backdoors: the Pardon, Article Zero and the Undertally itself.

UI Visual Key

  • Public Tally: translucent ice-blue panels with thin gold borders and a lantern sigil.
  • Undertally: black-glass panels with violet text that drips like ink. Undertow appears as a vertical column of violet water.
  • Stakefire: a floating gold contract framed in living flame.
  • Chime SFX: always written TING-TA-LING.
4. Protagonist: Jonah Reed, Known as "Wren Calloway" and "the Hush"

Everyone calls him Wren until Ch 40. The captions carry Jonah's inner voice.

Background. On Earth he is 24, a world-record speedrunner with the handle "Stillwater," famous because his face never moves, even on world records. His mother, the indie designer Miriam Reed, died when he was 11. She left behind a six-level prototype labeled for jonah & lily (unfinished). Their father went quiet, so Jonah raised his sister Lily, who was 4 at the time. He didn't cry at the funeral because Lily was holding his hand and "someone had to be still." He hasn't cried since. Every anniversary he plays her prototype in one silent, perfect run. On the 13th anniversary he ignores weeks of chest pain from an undiagnosed heart defect and dies at the final frame, with Lily's unread text on his phone: "call me after your run?"

Starting weakness. He begins as a Silt Wretch at Lv 1: a 16-year-old corpse held together by Spill-mud, outside the Pale. He has no Tally and no weapon, and he is weaker than a Murmur. He also can't cry, so every feeling he swallows raises his Undertow.

Hidden persona vs. true self: - Mask 1, "Wren the Fluke": a polite, sleepy, aggressively average Null who "survived by luck." He scores exactly 60.00 on everything. - Mask 2, "the Hush": the silent, masked Calamity that kills Wracks and never makes a sound. - True self: in some ways still an 11-year-old standing at a funeral, running a no-hit run of his own life (take no damage, show no damage). He is fiercely protective and extremely competent, funny without meaning to be, and terrified of what happens if he ever lets go.

The misunderstandings: - Solenne thinks he's a genius hiding in plain sight. She's right, but for the wrong reasons. - Otto thinks the Hush is a tragic exiled prince working through a nine-step plan. There is no plan. - Iona thinks the Hush is a Calamity probing the city's defenses. - Tomorrow thinks he's a prophesied king of the Unwept. - The Unlit think "Gamer" is a holy title. - Severin thinks he's the Wickmother's agent. He is, without knowing it.

Final power level. As Fathom he is the only being the Tally could not count. He can hold, digest and return the emotional weight of an entire civilization. After the Tally falls he keeps his Depth. He has no numbers anymore but is still the strongest being in Orison, and he mostly uses that to calm storms, walk on still water and fix roofs.

Emotional arc: 1. Suppress (Arc 1) 2. Explode in a Capsize (Arc 2) 3. Feel in small doses through Digestion (Arc 3) 4. Say his anger and grief out loud (Arc 4) 5. Weep (Ch 39) 6. Live with feeling (Ch 40)

His Undertow ends at 0%, not 100%. Theme line: "Still water isn't water that never moves. It's water deep enough to hold the storm."

Appearance (keep identical in every prompt): - Human form: a lean, pale 16-year-old. Messy ash-black hair falls over his eyes, with one white streak at the left temple. Sleepy gray eyes glow violet as Undertow rises. A thin black vein-like scar runs from behind his right ear down his neck. Black gloves hide his violet-veined hands. He wears a charcoal-navy high-collared Lanternhall coat with brass lantern buttons and the gray "unlit lantern" Null patch on the left shoulder. His expression is always blank, and he's usually holding bread. - Earth (Ch 1): 24, with short black hair, brown eyes and dark circles, a gray hoodie and an over-ear headset. Same blank face. - The Hush (Riptide Stalker): a 3-meter, lean, predatory humanoid. Glossy black plating like wet obsidian with glowing violet seams. A smooth white bone mask with no mouth and two vertical violet eye-slits. A tattered mantle of shadow-tendrils like a drowned cloak. Long four-clawed hands. The mist goes perfectly still around him. - Maelstrom Knight: 3.5 meters, with layered obsidian knight-plates, a spiral horn crest sweeping back from the mask, a halberd of compressed black water, and a mantle that turns in a slow vortex. - Deepwarden: a 30-meter colossus of black tide and plating, with a whale-like skull mask, current-like tendrils, and violet bioluminescent constellations along the ribs. - Capsize: a malformed Hush the size of a mountain, its mask cracked down the center and covered in dozens of eye-slits. It is completely silent. - Fathom: human-sized, with a body like still night water reflecting stars: deep blue-black with gold and violet points of light inside it. A slow gold ripple-halo sits behind his head. His own face shows through, calm, with gold-violet eyes.

1. Solenne Holloway, "the Ice Lantern" (16, Beacon, Lv 63, Yield 78%) - Look: long straight silver-white hair in a high ponytail tied with a black ribbon; pale ice-blue eyes; a small beauty mark under the left eye; a white-and-gold Beacon honors uniform with a short white shoulder cape; a slender white-gold rapier, Matins, with a lantern-shaped guard. A cracked iron lantern sits where the head should be, burning with violet flame. Tattered green Vigil banners form its cape, and it carries a colossal broken-tipped greatsword, Homeward. It speaks in a chorus of hundreds of voices. - Origin and motivation: Tomorrow is 312 years of soldiers' siphoned pre-battle fear, condensed around a single sentence: "I'll be home tomorrow." It has to hold the line, but it no longer knows for whom. - Arc: Arc 2 antagonist, then rival general, then loyal general. She wears a deep green Vigil longcoat with silver lantern insignia and carries a lantern-headed glaive, Last Watch. - Role: authority, then hunter of the Hush, then reluctant savior, then defector, then mentor, then sacrifice. - Motivation: Guilt over every Snuffing order she has signed, including Wren's. She refused the Pyre Grading Rite because she could feel what it would take from her. - Ends: She dies holding the Wick's gate. 7. High Tallier Severin Ashgrave (300+, Pyre, Lv 99, later Zenith). The main antagonist. - Look: tall and gaunt, appearing about 60. Long straight white hair tied at the nape, colorless pale-gray eyes, immaculate white high-collared robes embroidered with gold Tally sigils, a thin gold circlet, and white gloves that never come off. Zenith form: porcelain skin with fine gold cracks, six wings of white lamplight, and a slowly rotating halo of Tally windows. - Motivation: He lost his wife and daughter in the Unmaking and begged the Wickmother to take the grief away. His Yield has been 100% ever since. He believes feeling is the disease that ended the world, and he isn't wrong that it did. - Ends: He loses the Article Zero Stakefire and gets his Knot back. He remembers his daughter's name, Elodie, weeps, and crumbles to dust holding onto it.

8. Miriam Reed, the Wickmother - Look: In memories and dev-logs: late 30s, warm brown eyes, dark brown hair in a loose bun with a pencil stuck through it, an oversized oatmeal cardigan and an ink smudge on one cheek. In the Wick: suspended in white-gold crystal with her hair floating and her eyes closed, threads of light streaming from her chest into the spire. - Role: the central mystery, and Jonah's mother. - Ends: She weeps with her son, dismantles her own system and fades with the Wick's light. She spends her last spark sending a dream across the dark to Lily.

Supporting characters - Crumb: a palm-sized puff of black mist with two white dot eyes and four stubby legs. It squeaks "mip" and is afraid of everything. It is secretly the last feelings of the real Wren. - Granny Vesk: the one-eyed elder of the Unlit, with a clay pipe and a patchwork shawl. 6. The 40-Chapter Outline

ARC 1: UNLIT (Ch 1–10)

Arc twist (Ch 10): the monsters are made of the city's own people.

Ch 1 – The Anniversary Run. On the 13th anniversary of his mother's death, Jonah streams his yearly silent run of her six-level prototype. His chest aches and his sister's text sits unanswered. He hits the final frame and his heart stops. A window appears: [Soul caught. Body: deceased. Substituting.] He wakes in black-violet mist inside a corpse wearing the tag WREN CALLOWAY · UNLIT. A Murmur sniffs him and moves on, unable to find a single feeling. On instinct he swallows a Knot it dropped, and the chime rings: TING-TA-LING. It's his mother's chime.

Ch 2 – Silt. Wracks hunt emotion, and one moment of panic nearly kills him. The Undertally opens and shows the UNDERTOW gauge. He reads a Wail's lunge cycle frame by frame, binds Stillness ("So my resting face is a build"), and kills it by taking a deliberate hit to launch himself off a ledge. In Wren's pocket he finds a diary: "June, I'm sorry I wasn't enough." His tenth Knot evolves him into a Gnawling. A terrified Wrackling he names Crumb refuses to leave him.

Ch 3 – Thirty Nights. A survival montage planned like a speedrun route. He sleeps inside a dead Threnody's ribcage, steals Dread Veil and Blink Step, and binds the Bread Clause. In a drowned city he finds murals of seven crowned kings and a weeping woman falling from the sky. On Night 30 he evolves into a Riptide Stalker, which lets him fold the monster inside and wear Wren's human face. He reaches the Pale, a 300-meter wall of white light.

Ch 4 – Clipping Through Heaven. He finds a 3-frame gap in each of the Pale's pulses and Blink-clips through, like a glitch that takes a game character out of bounds. Commander Iona, who signed Wren's exile, goes gray at the sight of him. The never-used Pardon of Thirty Nights forces the Concord to pardon him and enroll him at Lanternhall, and the city nicknames him "the Fluke." June slams into him sobbing, and he can't cry back. Undertow +8%. She studies his face a beat too long.

Ch 5 – Exactly Sixty. The public Tally check shows UNLIT, and the hall laughs. Otto talks for fourteen panels straight. Dorian picks the Null as his new hobby. Solenne looks straight through everyone. Wren scores exactly 60.00 on all five entrance exams. Solenne: "Nobody gets exactly sixty by accident." In the Crown, a white-gloved hand turns a report labeled NULL RETURNED.

Ch 6 – Article Zero. Dorian lights a Stakefire to get Wren re-exiled. Wren reads the charter like a manual and pauses on Article Zero. As the challenged party he writes the rules: a duel "until one party yields or cannot continue." He never attacks. He sidesteps every flame strike by centimeters while eating an apple, until Dorian's Thrum runs dry. His prize is that Dorian must eat lunch with Otto once a week for a year. Solenne rewatches the fight frame by frame.

Ch 7 – It Tripped. On a field exercise under Iona ("The price of Pyre was too high"), a Dirge ambushes a lost squad in the fog. Wren slips away, stacks Stillness, the Bread Clause and The Window at ×9, and erases it with one blow. Solenne finds the shattered Knot with Wren standing next to it, holding a bread roll. "...It tripped." Neither of them blinks.

Ch 8 – Counterfeit. The Auditors announce a Discrepancy Sweep. Wren hunts an Envy-Wrack through the sewers and steals Counterfeit. During a class demonstration it glitches and shows "Grade: LANTERN" for one second, because Dorian's window was the last one he copied. Otto faints. In June's shop she grumbles about "pressure lines" that run out of the city and connect to nothing. Crumb hides in her toolbox, and she pretends not to notice.

Ch 9 – The Ninth Bell. A Lament breaches the Outer Ward and eight bells ring as it heads for June's block. Wren lets the monster out in public for the first time: a silent, masked hunter that takes the Lament apart with Blink-cancels. The panicking bell-ringer rings a ninth bell that doesn't exist. By dawn the city has a legend, the Hush. Undertow is at 61%. On a rooftop, Otto finds his calling.

Ch 10 – The Woman in the Red Scarf. Otto founds the Order of the Hush with three members and one pin. Wren gnaws the Lament's Knot and lives its memory: a mother's grief for her son Tobin, who drowned in a cistern, along with a red scarf and a lullaby. The next morning at the market he sees Maren Adair alive and smiling, wearing the scarf, with no memory of ever having a child. The Wracks are made of the city's people. Splash panel: "The monsters outside the walls are us." Undertow is at 68%.

ARC 2: THE HUSH (Ch 11–20)

Arc twist (Ch 19–20): Grades measure how much feeling you've surrendered, the Harvest is a farm, and the Hush has Wren's face.

Ch 11 – The Order Convenes. The Order meets under Wren's bed. Otto presents a nine-step theory of the Hush's master plan, and Wren calls it "compelling." Iona forms a task force to capture the Hush and drafts Solenne. Wren buys bread from Maren every morning. He is the only person who knows what she lost.

Ch 12 – Ice Lantern. Solenne's chapter. She spars with Wren daily, and he "loses" every bout by exactly one point. On day nine her feint lands, and his eyes flash violet for a single frame. "You're hiding something. I'm going to find it." Undertow is at 72%, and his window reads [Evolution blocked: condition unmet].

Ch 13 – The Grading Trials. Otto signs Wren up for the Trials "as a surprise." Wren tries to lose and keeps advancing, because his rivals keep falling into the exact holes he's casually walking around. Dorian trains until his palms bleed. His grandfather visits, wearing white gloves and disappointment.

Ch 14 – The Rule-Labyrinth. The second round is a Stakefire maze where every broken rule burns Grade. Wren has no Grade to burn, so he walks straight through the rule-walls. He rescues Dorian from a rigged trap, and Dorian hates him more for it. The trap shows that the Auditors are using the Trials to hunt Discrepancies.

Ch 15 – Discrepancy. An Auditor's True Read pierces Counterfeit. Wren buries it under forty stacked fake windows (pop-up spam) until the Auditor's lens cracks. That night June shows him a blueprint: the conduits run from every home's Tally-shrine out through the Pale. "The Tally doesn't just measure us. It takes something."

Ch 16 – Tomorrow. Wren follows the conduits to the Weeping Vents and watches Wracks condense out of the mist as they're born. There he meets Tomorrow. He is outclassed and barely escapes. "You smell like us, little silence. Why do you wear their face?"

Ch 17 – Ring-Out. In the semifinal against Solenne he can't win without exposing himself and can't lose obviously without drawing suspicion. He engineers a ring-out in which both of them leave the arena on the same frame. Dorian wins the Trials by default, and the trophy tastes like ash. "You matched my timing to the frame." "I slipped." Severin orders an audit of the Calloway file.

Ch 18 – The Harvest Bell. The Concord announces the Harvest: the Pale will be lowered for one night. Iona breaks into the sealed archives and finds that every past Tide matched a siphon surge, which means they were scheduled. June is posted to the breach crew. On a rooftop, Solenne says only "Show me." He doesn't. Undertow is at 91%.

Ch 19 – Capsize. The Pale drops. Tomorrow's Tide pours in, the siphons scream at full draw, and June and Dorian are both trapped. Undertow hits 100% and he CAPSIZES: a mountain-sized Hush crushes the Tide and a kilometer of wall in total silence. In the rubble, Solenne watches the mask split and sees Wren's face.

Ch 20 – Beyond the Pale, Again. He collapses back into a broken, smoking boy. Solenne raises her rapier, and for the first time in her life her hand shakes. The Concord names him the Silent Calamity and orders his execution. Iona opens a gap in the Pale instead: "I signed your exile once. I'll sign it twice. Run." One of the Knots he swallowed during the Capsize belonged to a Concord elder, and it proves the Concord knows everything. He walks into the Spill with Crumb, his Undertow crashed to 40%.

ARC 3: STILLWATER (Ch 21–30)

Arc twist (Ch 30): the Wickmother is alive inside the Wick, and she is Jonah's mother.

Ch 21 – The Unlit. Half-dead, he is found by Snuffed Nulls who have survived in the ruins, some of them half-mad from eating raw Knots. Granny Vesk watches him tear a Dirge apart with his bare hands and asks what he is. "...A gamer." By nightfall, "the Gamer" is a holy title.

Ch 22 – Civilization Speedrun. He builds from a mental tech tree: sand-and-charcoal water filters, fungus farms, germ theory and latrines, windmills made from wreckage, a pulley crane and a ring of trenches. Wherever he sleeps, the Spill stills into a black mirror lake. He mutters "stillwater," and the settlement has its name. In Lanthorn, Otto uses June's maintenance pass to slip out and "rescue Wren from the Hush."

Ch 23 – Digestion. Vesk teaches him that Knots are feelings meant to be felt, not stored. He relives Maren's grief and lets it hurt. He can't cry, but he shakes. [Knot Digested.] [Hidden stat unlocked: DEPTH.] He evolves into the Maelstrom Knight (Lv 75). Undertow drops to 31%. He begins teaching the Unlit to digest, and they become his first warriors.

Ch 24 – Roommate. Otto arrives and discovers that the Hush is his roommate. His meltdown goes through five stages: denial, fainting, screaming, "You READ my theories?!", and silence. Then the real hurt: "You let me think you were dead." Wren apologizes and says what he feels out loud for the first time (Undertow −5%). Otto kneels as Stillwater's first sworn follower, and the Order becomes a real spy network.

Ch 25 – Siege of Lanterns. Tomorrow's legions surround Stillwater, intending to crown the Silent Calamity or devour him. Wren lights a Stakefire war-game played with real units on a ruined plain. Tomorrow writes the rules: "A commander loses when no unit of theirs remains on the field." It carries three centuries of soldiers' instincts and dominates the first half.

Ch 26 – Checkmate in the Dark. Wren baits Tomorrow's fear-born urge to protect its flanks, exploits the turn order, and sacrifices his whole army on purpose. His last surviving unit is Crumb, which has been hiding inside Tomorrow's own lantern-head since the opening parley. Tomorrow cannot win without shattering its own head. While it hesitates, Wren speaks to the soldiers inside: "You can go home tomorrow." Tomorrow kneels, and the Unwept join Stillwater.

Ch 27 – The Heir Who Lost. Dorian finds his grandfather's ledger and learns that Severin hollowed out Dorian's mother to raise Dorian's Grade. As he flees, he saves June from Auditors inside a conduit, along with her blueprints. At Stillwater he draws his sword on Wren, then drops it and asks for help. He binds a loyalty Tether. Crumb nearly explodes with joy at the sight of June.

Ch 28 – Envoy of Ice. Solenne arrives as the Concord's envoy, escorted by Iona's unit with assassins hidden among them. By the lake she admits she can't stop thinking about the face under the mask and doesn't know what the feeling is called. Wren stops the assassins without a single death. Iona defects. Solenne goes back to the city as a double agent. Undertow is at 22%.

Ch 29 – The Pyre Legion. Severin's Pyre Legion attacks with siphon-lances. Stillwater holds the line with trebuchets, mirror-signal towers, Dorian's tactics, Iona's veterans, the Unwept and Nulls who can now digest Knots. When a thousand people who were free to flee choose to stand behind him, he evolves into the Deepwarden (30 meters tall, Lv 120). They win, at a cost.

Ch 30 – The Wickmother. The Legion's war-standard is a reliquary holding the First Knot, the first Yield ever taken. When Wren digests it he feels a mother's grief for the two children she left behind on another world, and he finds a hidden dev-log inside it: "If you're seeing this, kiddo, you found my backdoor." It's Miriam Reed. Then Severin addresses the world: in nine days the Final Tally will siphon every feeling from every human, permanently. Undertow jumps from 22% to 87% in a single panel.

ARC 4: FATHOM (Ch 31–40)

Arc twist (Ch 37): Severin built the Harvest to make Jonah Capsize. Everything Jonah suppressed became the fuel for the Final Tally.

Ch 31 – Anger Is Also a Feeling. He is furious at his mother for dying, for building this and for dragging him here, and he feels guilty about Lily. Undertow reaches 94% and the lake begins to boil. June tells him she always knew he wasn't her brother and chose him anyway: "You can be angry at her and still save her." He screams for the first time in thirteen years and punches a cliff in half. Undertow drops to 55%. "...I'll fix that."

Ch 32 – Council of the Unlikely. Stillwater becomes a nation, governed by a granny, a fanboy, a disgraced heir, a defector, a 13-year-old and a Wrack. They try to crown Wren. He declines, so they vote him "Warden" over his objections. Otto's intel says the city is going hollow, and Maren has forgotten her own name.

Ch 33 – Solenne's Knot. Solenne's own father has her strapped to a total-siphon. Wren infiltrates the city through a new desync in the Pale's pulse, rescues her, and returns her Knot from the vault: everything that was taken from her since she was 12. The Ice Lantern weeps. Her Grade collapses to Unlit, and her light comes back warm.

Ch 34 – The Day the Pale Fell. Severin drops the Pale entirely and drives every Wrack in the Spill at the city, because terror feeds the siphon. Stillwater comes to defend the people who exiled them. The Unwept shield children, and the Hush stands on the walls. Maren sees the Hush and doesn't run.

Ch 35 – Strand's Last Order. Iona holds the Wick's gate alone so the others can get inside. In her last words she says she knows he isn't the boy she exiled, and she apologizes to both of them. Wren grieves out loud and doesn't break. [Undertow converting → Depth.] Her glaive is left standing in the gate.

Ch 36 – Inside the Wick. The Wick's six tiers are his mother's six prototype levels. "I've beaten this four thousand times." He speedruns them. Dorian duels his grandfather's guard, Otto and June sabotage the conduits, and Tomorrow holds the bridge. At the summit, Miriam hangs suspended in crystal while Severin rises above her as a Zenith.

Ch 37 – Zenith. Severin rewrites the rules mid-fight. He disables Blink, reverses gravity and voids every Tether except Stillness, the one that keeps Jonah sealed. The Deepwarden shatters. Severin reveals the Harvest plan and pours the entire harvest into Jonah to force a final Capsize. Undertow reaches 99%. Jonah chooses neither stillness nor explosion and lets himself feel. His face moves. [Tether "Stillness" broken. SNAP incoming.]

Ch 38 – Fathom. [...Snap absorbed by DEPTH.] [Evolution condition met: Feel everything. Hold nothing back. Hold no one down.] He becomes FATHOM, and Undertow falls to 0%. He digests the harvest and starts returning feelings to their owners slowly, like a tide coming in rather than a wave. Then he invokes Article Zero: "If you feel nothing, tell me your daughter's name." Severin can't, and he loses control of the system. Jonah returns his Knot. "...Elodie." Severin weeps three hundred years too late and crumbles to dust.

Ch 39 – Credits. Miriam wakes. "You got so tall." He gives her back the First Knot and says everything he couldn't say at her funeral. Jonah cries for the first time in thirteen years, and she cries with him. Together they shut down the Tally like closing a save file. The Pale dissolves, and real sunlight reaches Orison for the first time in 312 years while the panels scroll like end credits. Miriam fades and sends her last spark to Lily as a dream. Crumb returns to June, and she finally grieves her real brother while holding her new brother's hand. Tomorrow's chorus says "We're home."

Ch 40 – Stillwater Runs Deep. One year later there is one nation, with no Grades and no Tally. People grieve, rage and laugh out loud, and Null "Fathomers" sit with anyone whose storm gets too big. Solenne is Speaker. Dorian sits with his mother, Otto publishes his book, and Maren visits Tobin's grave. The people vote to make him King. He declines, so they name the lake after him, and he accepts that because lakes don't attend meetings. He tells everyone his real name. On his mother's anniversary he doesn't play the game. He sits on the dock and tells his friends about her and Lily, laughing and crying. One last window appears: [Achievement Unlocked: Stillwater Runs Deep.] [Thank you for playing.] It closes forever. THE END.

Planned epilogue: On Earth, years later, Lily Reed wakes from a dream of a lake at sunrise. She finishes their mother's prototype and adds a seventh level: a still lake where two figures wave.

7. Originality Check

Elements that were too close to existing works, and what I changed:

Too close to Element Change made
Attack on Titan (walls, monsters that were human, a hero who shifts into one); From the New World The Pale, Wracks, the Hush There are no walls, only a pulsing dome of light. Wracks were never people: they are people's exported feelings, and those people are still alive. His transformation comes from absorbed emotion, not bloodline or injection.
Jujutsu Kaisen (monsters born from human negative emotion) Wracks The feelings don't leak out naturally. An engineered ranking system extracts them. Each Knot holds one living person's memory, and the solution is to return it, not destroy it. It's revealed as a twist, not stated as the premise.
Madoka Magica (emotion harvested for energy) The siphon There are no contracts, no alien harvesters and no individual transformation. It's an emergency system built by a human that grew into a class hierarchy.
Reincarnated as a Slime and So I'm a Spider (weakest monster, evolves by eating, founds a nation) The evolution line and Stillwater His body is a human corpse. Eating Knots gives emotion-skills that carry a psychological cost. Evolutions are gated by emotional conditions. The nation is built mostly by exiled humans, and the system's creator is his mother, not a god.
Solo Leveling (secret leveling, a shadow army, "Monarch" titles) Forms and Tidecall The stage I first drafted as "Abyssal Sovereign" is now Deepwarden. There are no gates and no raising the dead. Tidecall only works on Wracks that chose him.
Eminence in Shadow and Overlord (misunderstood mastermind, worshipful over-readers) The Hush and the Order He isn't playing a role; he's trying to be invisible. The cult's founder doesn't know who he is. The misunderstandings come from his emotional flatness, and the wrong theories accidentally build a real spy network.
Hunter × Hunter vows; Jujutsu Kaisen binding vows and power boosts from revealing your ability Tethers I dropped any power boost for revealing your ability. Tethers are priced by how often an average person would fail them, which creates the difficulty-arbitrage exploit, and breaking one causes a Snap.
Mob Psycho 100 (an emotion meter that explodes at 100%) Undertow Undertow is a system stat paired with Depth. It works as a damage trap, 100% triggers a monster Capsize, and the arc ends at 0%.
No Game No Life (a world governed by games) Stakefire I renamed it from "Gambit." It's one legal tool in a violent world, and what matters most is a single backdoor clause.
Shangri-La Frontier and Sword Art Online (a gamer exploiting a game world) Jonah's edge Orison is not a game. His advantage is timing arbitrage and reading rules literally, not knowing a game's content.
Dr. Stone (rebuilding with science) Arc 3 It's three chapters of practical survival tech in a sunless mist, framed as base-building, not a science-kingdom saga.
Black Clover, Mashle, The Irregular at Magic High School (powerless outcast) Null "Null" doesn't mean powerless; it means the siphon can't take from you. The rank measures emptiness, so the bottom of the ladder is the most human.
Hunter × Hunter (a parent who designed a game); Overlord (earlier transmigrators founding nations) Miriam She died on Earth, rebuilt her prototype to survive a catastrophe, and was imprisoned by her own system. Her story is a tragedy, not an adventure.

Names changed while drafting: - "the Lamplighter" became the Wickmother, because Lamplighter is a known superhero name. - "Seraphine" became Solenne, because Seraphine is a famous game character. - The top Wrack class "Requiem" became Threnody, because of JoJo. - "Gambit" became Stakefire. - "Abyssal Sovereign" became Deepwarden.

Coined terms I checked and kept: Tally, Undertally, Thrum, Knot, Yield, Marks, Lattice, Tether, Snap, Stakefire, Undertow, Depth, Capsize, Gnaw, Digest, the Pale, the Spill, Wrack, Unwept, Murmur→Threnody, Tinder→Zenith, Lanthorn, Orison, the Wick, Lanternhall, the Snuffing, Article Zero. I found no matching named system, place or organization in existing anime, manga, manhwa or light novels. "Stillwater," "Hush" and "Unwept" are ordinary English words, and "unwept" also appears in public-domain poetry.

📜 Continuity note
  • Jonah Reed is no longer Tallied. He keeps his Depth, without numbers. He can still calm storms and walk on still water, and he mostly fixes roofs. He's still restacking the cliff he punched. He told everyone his real name. He laughs and cries out loud, and he smiled for the first time. Undertow: gone. The Tally: gone.
  • The world: Lanthorn and Stillwater are one nation, connected by a road, with no Grades, no Tally and no Pale. The Spill is gone, and there's real sunlight. Feelings still sometimes make small weather, and Fathomers sit with people until the storm passes. The three laws stand.
  • Resolutions:
  • Solenne: First Speaker. She laughs openly. She told Jonah "the word."
  • Dorian: Knight-Commander of a Vigil that protects instead of reaping. He spends time with his mother, who is awake again. He still eats Thursday lunch with Otto.
  • Otto: author of the bestseller The Hush and I, with footnotes on every one of Jonah's denials.
  • June: Chief Engineer, age 14. She has grieved Wren, and she calls Jonah "Jonah Reed-Calloway."
  • Cassius: runs the Returning Office, giving back three centuries of Yield.
  • Maren: remembers Tobin and visits his grave in the red scarf.
  • Kit: loud again.
  • Vesk: taught the first Fathomer class.
  • Moth: seven, and she has her own sling.
  • Mags: runs the kitchen.
  • Bellwether: drums at weddings.
  • Iona: Last Watch is her monument, and the new Vigil oath ends with "Just home."
  • Brannoch: Brannoch's Mill, "It's Quiet Here."
  • Tomorrow: returned home. Homeward stands by the lake.
  • Severin: at peace, with Elodie.
  • Miriam: faded. Her last window appeared on the anniversary.
  • The lake is named "LAKE JONAH." He accepted, because lakes don't attend meetings.
  • The final window: "Achievement Unlocked: Stillwater Runs Deep. Thank you for playing. — M.R." Then it closed forever.

Series resolution checklist

  • The central mystery: Wracks are made of exported feeling. The Tally is a siphon built from Miriam's game. The Wickmother is Jonah's mother. All of it has been answered and resolved, with the Tally shut down, the feelings returned and real sunlight restored.
  • The main antagonist: Severin lost the Article Zero Stakefire, remembered Elodie, and died at peace.
  • The rivalries:
  • Dorian: rival, then defector, then sworn knight. He got his anger back and reunited with his mother.
  • Solenne: rival, then investigator, then double agent, then partner. Her Knot was returned.
  • Tomorrow: enemy, then general, then returned home.
  • Hask: killed by Iona.
  • Jonah's emotional arc: he suppressed his feelings, Capsized, learned to digest, named his anger and grief, wept, and learned to live with feeling. His Undertow ended at 0%, not 100%.
  • Lily: the thread on Earth was resolved through the dream and the finished game.
